overview.title: Craft under a palace roof
overview.p1: Dar Jamai was a late-19th-century palace before it became the museum of Moroccan arts in Meknes. Inside you find ceramics, woodwork, textiles and the domestic scale of elite life — a useful counterpoint to the monumental gates and granaries outside.
overview.p2: The building itself matters: courtyards, rooms and the way light falls on displayed objects. It is an indoor stop when heat or fatigue hits, and a way to understand what the souks outside still produce in living form.
overview.p3: Visit after a medina loop or before lunch. Tickets are modest; time needed is under two hours unless you read every label slowly.

q1.question: Is there an entry fee?
q1.answer: Yes — standard museum ticket. Check current prices at the desk.

q2.question: How long do I need?
q2.answer: One to one and a half hours is comfortable for most visitors.

q3.question: Is it good in the heat?
q3.answer: Yes — it is one of the best indoor pauses in historic Meknes.

q4.question: Are labels in several languages?
q4.answer: Often in Arabic and French; English may be limited. A simple guide booklet helps if available.

q5.question: Where is it relative to Place el-Hedim?
q5.answer: On the edge of the medina, a short walk from the square.

food.title: Café nearby after the museum
food.p1: Exit toward Place el-Hedim or the medina for tea and a light meal. The museum itself is for looking, not dining.
food.p2: Combine with a souk walk so the objects you saw indoors connect to stalls outside.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Dar Jamai Museum

1.title: Use it as a heat and fatigue reset
1.desc: If the square and souks have drained you, Dar Jamai gives shade, structure and a clear end point. It is more restorative than forcing another outdoor monument in harsh light.

2.title: Look at the building, not only the cases
2.desc: Ceilings, doors and courtyard proportions explain elite Meknes as much as the objects. Slow down in the empty corners.

3.title: Pair with the medina the same half-day
3.desc: Morning souks, museum late morning, lunch after — a clean sequence that avoids backtracking across town.
